A letter from the head
Choosing your child’s school is one of the most important decisions you will make and I understand the weight of that responsibility. I often compare choosing the right school to choosing the right home. Your child’s school will be their home away from home, and it needs to be somewhere they will be happy, they will thrive, and they will grow.
At St. Aubyn’s, we believe deeply in our motto, Bravely, Faithfully, Happily. We promise to challenge every child to be brave in their thinking and ambitious in their goals. We promise to develop citizens who act with integrity, compassion and responsibility. And we promise to create an environment where happiness is not a by-product but a foundation.
The results speak for themselves: 100% of our pupils who sat the 11+ in 2025 received an offer from one of their chosen senior schools, and our three-year average stands at 97%. What I am most proud of is how our children achieve those results – with confidence, with kindness, and with a genuine love of learning.
The happiness of and wellbeing of our pupils also speaks for itself. As I walk around the school from time to time, I am greeted by pupils who want to be here, want to learn, and want to do their very best.
St. Aubyn’s is the perfect size, too. It’s small enough for staff to know each child individually, large and ambitious enough for them to try everything that we have on offer.
The best way to understand what makes us different is to visit. Come and see our children learning, our teachers teaching, and our community in action. We will be delighted to discuss with you how our wider partnership as a member of the Bancroft’s Family of Schools feeds into the individual experience all of our pupils enjoy.
I look forward to welcoming you personally.
Louis Taylor
Head of St. Aubyn’s School

More about St. Aubyn’s
Dedicated to nurturing curious minds.
Through innovative teaching methods and a dynamic curriculum, we empower every child to reach their full potential and become lifelong learners and contributors to society. We embrace diversity, champion inquiry, and cultivate a culture of respect, empathy, and resilience.
Find out more about applying to our school
St. Aubyn’s is one of the oldest schools of its type in the country, founded in January 1884 by James Crump BA.
It was originally sited opposite Bancroft’s School and in 1893 moved to premises on the site of the present Hawkey Hall. In 1919 the school was relocated to its current site in Bunces Lane, with a temporary relocation to Cumberland during the Second World War.
In 1922, Colonel W H Colley took over the School and in 1951 his son, Mr H H Colley, joined the staff. Mr Harold Colley took over as Headmaster in 1967 and in 1975 the School became a registered charity, St. Aubyn’s, Woodford Green, School Trust. Mr Harold Colley retired in 1993 and was succeeded by Headmaster, Mr Gordon James MA (Oxon) in whose time the School doubled in size and saw the introduction of girls. Mr James retired in 2013 to be succeeded by Mr Leonard Blom. During this time, the School benefitted from significant developmental changes: a new Dining Hall, Nursery building, extension to the Performing Arts Centre, Reception conservatory to name but a few. It also went from strength to strength in its academic achievements.
Mr Blom retired in 2023, with his successor being Mr Taylor.
The Bancroft’s Family of Schools was established in 2026, it brings together Bancroft’s, St. Aubyn’s School, and Woodford Green Preparatory School. Each school remains proudly itself, while wider opportunities for pupils, families and staff bring benefits of collective strength that come from working together.
A more detailed account of the School’s history can be found below. This was written by former pupil and school archivist, Nicholas Dixon. The School Archive may be of interest to anyone wishing to know more of the School’s history and we are always grateful for any information, memorabilia etc., relating to our past.

All pupils from Nursery to Year 6 participate in music and drama. The performing arts are not reserved for the talented few – they are a fundamental part of how we build confidence, self-expression and creative thinking across the school.
Our purpose-built performing arts centre, dedicated Drama and Dance Studio, and a programme of termly concerts, annual productions and instrumental tuition provide every child with the opportunity to discover and develop their creative talents.

Music for all
Led by Ms Penny Manser (Head of Music), the music department aims to provide a musical education that is available to all pupils, not just the musically elite. The department is housed in the purpose-built Performing Arts Centre, which includes a main music classroom, a performance hall, a smaller practice room, three individual practice rooms and office space.
Co-curricular music groups include orchestra, string ensemble, two choirs, brass ensemble, woodwind ensemble, and guitar group. Performance opportunities span church services, termly concerts, instrumental concerts, assemblies, the house singing competition, local festivals and music-related trips and competitions throughout the year.
Individual instrumental tuition is available from 15 peripatetic instrumental teachers who visit throughout the week, covering a wide range of instruments.

Drama and confidence
Performing in public is a transformative experience for children – and one that builds lasting confidence. Drama at St. Aubyn’s supports all-round educational development and is woven into the curriculum from the earliest years.
Led by Mrs Lisa Beckley, the drama programme ranges from class assemblies for younger pupils through to character roles in the numerous annual productions that are a highlight of the school calendar. Productions span Early Years nativities, class performances and ambitious musicals staged in the performing arts centre.
Visiting actors and theatre groups regularly support drama skill delivery, and drama forms an integral part of the literacy curriculum – bringing texts to life and developing pupils’ spoken English, empathy and creative interpretation.

Dance is part of the PE curriculum for Years 3, 4 and 5, introducing pupils to exercise, fitness and choreographic thinking. Pupils learn the elements of dance and explore theme-based and pupil-led choreography.

St. Aubyn’s school society (SASS)
An integral and valued partner to the school
We are a group of interested parents and staff bringing about events and initiatives to benefit the lives of the families and staff at our school.
We are committed to enriching the community spirit of our school.
One of the ways we do this is by running a busy calendar of events throughout the school year. We have annual events such as Fireworks and Camp Night and others that we alternate each year, such as the Circus and the Summer Fete.
The money we raise is used to purchase items to help the school. We have funded the purchase of minibuses, tiered seating in the PAC, a secret playground for Pre-Prep, improved wi-fi, iPads and digital cameras. We even funded the outdoor amphitheatre, which was completed in 2017.
SASS Initiatives
The SASS Initiatives are there to improve the experience of the pupils, staff and families at St. Aubyn’s. These initiatives are the little touches brought about to help either parents, children or staff on a more regular basis.
SASS set up and runs the enormously successful second hand uniform shop which reuses hundreds of good quality items of uniform each year. It is located in the wooden building between the main entrance and the Nursery. Opening times are advertised to parents. This is an enormously valuable resource for our parents.
SASS also contributes to seasonal gifts for the children (Christmas and Easter), provides the annual Christmas trees and makes a significant contribution to the Year 6 leavers’ party each year.
We also look to our network of reps to help with refreshments for various school events and hold a start of term coffee morning to welcome parents back to the new term and inform them of the upcoming events.

Travelling safely to and from school
Safety is for our kids are also a top priority
Our pupils come from a large catchment area with many of them living too far from School to walk in.
As a result, many of our pupils travel to School by car. We try to encourage safe and considerate parking, walking and cycling to School.
Recent initiatives are detailed below.
Parking
‘Park and Stride’ is a scheme designed to reduce traffic around schools. The idea is that parents park at least five minutes from School and pupils walk the remaining distance. A Walking Zone Map can be downloaded by clicking the button below.
Parents can purchase a permit to use the Borough car parks at School drop off and pick up times (until 4:15 pm). The cost is just £35 for a year. The nearest car park is in Derby Road which is approximately a six minute walk from School. The Hawkey Hall car park to the North is approximately a twelve minute walk from School.
There is an agreement with Salway Church (at the top of Forest Approach) allowing parents to park in the Church car park to the left of the main entrance, the side furthest from Forest Approach. Parents and carers may park here entering and exiting the car park from the High Road only from 8.15 to 9.00 am and 3.15 to 4.15 pm, but only in term time. There is no arrangement for parking at lunchtime.

On the first Friday of every month, we hold a workshop and coffee morning led by Mrs Charlotte Six-Rais, the Head of Learning Support, covering a variety of topics.
Sessions are focused on learning and sharing knowledge, as well as personal experiences. Together, we enhance the tools in our kit to navigate the experiences of our children, from executive function through to emotional regulation.
Here you can access the slides from each workshop, to reflect on the statistics shared, the latest research, helpful links, and advice shared.
Upcoming workshops:
We encourage you to attend as many sessions as are relevant to your child(ren). The opportunity to sign up for workshops is shared via parent emails and the school newsletter. Upcoming topics include Understanding and increasing intrinsic motivation, Brain development: why kids “flip their lids”, Playground politics: understanding and managing conflict in friendships and Social communication & speech and language.
Explore our past workshops:

Growth Mindset and Intrinsic Motivation
During this session, we look into what a growth mindset is and why it matters, how intrinsic motivation supports long-term success, strategies to encourage resilience and independence at home and ways to help children respond positively to challenge and setbacks.
Phonics – Reading and Writing
This parent workshop explores Phonics – Reading and Writing. This workshop supports parents in understanding phonics throughout the development of their child’s skills and its essential role in reading and writing. We explore helpful tips to support your child at home and a selection of online resources.
Sibling Rivalry
This parent workshop explores Sibling Rivalry. We look at how parents can support their children to develop lasting relationships, points of tension between siblings, according to personality traits and age, and, as always, supportive tips that can be used at home during arguments and conflict, as well as creating activities that bring them closer together.
Child Development
This parent workshop explores Child Development and the four key areas of progression: physical, language, cognition and social/emotional alonside age milestones. Parents are provided with tools and prompts to use at home to continue supporting children’s development.
Routine
This parent workshop explores The Power of Routine. We explore why routines matter, examples of weekly routines and when they don’t go to plan.
Executive Functioning
This parent workshop explores Executive Function skills and how they impact learning, behaviour, and independence. Discover practical strategies to help your child develop focus, organisation, and problem-solving skills.
Maths anxiety vs Dyscalculia
This parent workshop focuses on exploring the difference between maths anxiety and dyscalculia. Learn how to recognise the signs of each and discover practical ways and strategies to support your child’s confidence and progress in maths.
Maths at St. Aubyn’s
This workshop explores our teaching approaches, policies, and strategies for supporting mathematical learning in both Pre-Prep and Prep. Learn how maths is taught across the school and how you can help at home.
E-Safety Workshop
For parents to explore common online worries and practical strategies for keeping children safe. We cover topics such as talking to your child, family rules, screen time, social media, and gaming.
Fine Motor Skills & Handwriting Workshop
A practical workshop exploring how children develop fine motor skills and handwriting. We’ll share strategies and activities you can use at home to support your child’s confidence and progress in these essential skills.
Mental Health Workshop
A workshop to explore the whole-school approach to mental health and wellbeing. This session will explore how we support pupils’ emotional resilience, promote positive relationships, and foster a healthy, balanced school environment. Parents will gain insight into the strategies used across the school, as well as within Place2Be, and how they can support their child’s wellbeing at home.

At St. Aubyn’s, wellbeing is not an alternative to academic rigour; it is what makes academic rigour sustainable. When children feel secure, understood and supported, they engage fully in learning, take confident risks and handle the demands of a selective academic environment.
Pastoral care here is proactive, personal and embedded into the fabric of the school. Every child is known as an individual, and our systems are designed to identify and respond to needs early.
